readerTitle: Cheap inquiries, expensive customers: how to compare channels
caseNote: 가상 사례 (산업용 철제 선반 제조사, 치과용 예약 소프트웨어) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 채널은 문의 한 건이 아니라 실제 고객 한 명을 얻는 비용, 그 고객의 가치, 그 채널이 더 데려올 수 있는 고객 수로 비교한다.
misconception: 문의(리드)를 가장 싸게, 가장 많이 가져오는 채널이 가장 좋은 채널이다.

sources.text: 마케팅의 표준 개념 (고객 획득 비용, 전환율, 고객 생애 가치)

factChecks.note: 소프트웨어 계산: 검색 광고 $5,000 ÷ 20명 = $250, 6개월 × $100 = $600 (약 2.4배). 협회 뉴스레터 $5,000 ÷ 15명 = 약 $333, 24개월 × $100 = $2,400 (약 7.2배). 가치는 단순화를 위해 매출 기준이며 원가와 할인율은 반영하지 않았습니다.
모든 수치는 가상입니다. 실제 업종 평균 전환율처럼 읽히지 않도록 카드에 illustrative 라벨을 유지하세요.

cards.title: Cheap inquiries, expensive customers
body: A small maker of steel warehouse shelving has $12,000 to spend on finding customers.
Online ads bring in inquiries for about $20 each. A trade show booth works out to about $200 per inquiry. One looks ten times cheaper. It isn't.

image.label: A cheap price tag on a pile of inquiries, a pricey tag on a few handshakes
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 왼쪽에 "$20" 가격표가 붙은 커다란 이메일 봉투 더미, 오른쪽에 "$200" 가격표가 붙은 작은 악수 아이콘 몇 개. 배경은 창고 선반. 실제 로고나 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Which channel won customers most cheaply?
body: You make custom steel shelving for warehouses. Here is what each $12,000 brought in last year:
Online ads: 600 inquiries, 1 in 100 bought. Direct mail to warehouse managers: 200 inquiries, 4 in 100 bought. A trade show: 60 inquiries, 15 in 100 bought.

options.text: Online ads. They bring ten times more inquiries for the money
options.feedback: Ads win on inquiries, but only 6 of 600 bought. Each customer cost $2,000, the most of the three.

options.text: Direct mail. A good balance of volume and quality
options.feedback: A solid middle: 8 customers at $1,500 each. Cheaper than ads, but not the cheapest.

options.text: The trade show, despite the fewest inquiries
options.feedback: Only 60 inquiries, but 9 became customers. That's about $1,333 each, the lowest of the three.

cards.title: The ranking flips.
body: Per inquiry, ads looked ten times cheaper than the show. Per paying customer, they were the most expensive channel.

image.label: The ranking flips.
image.brief: Labeled HTML chart from the lesson numbers

cards.title: Choosing channels by cost per customer
body: A **channel** is any route by which customers find you and buy: ads, shows, sales calls, shops, partners.
To choose between them, divide what you spent by the paying customers it brought. That's the **cost per customer**. Inquiries, clicks and visitors are steps on the way, not the result.
Then set that number against what a customer is worth to you.

image.label: Three funnels of different widths ending in similar drops
image.brief: 깔때기 3개를 나란히. 왼쪽(Online ads)은 입구가 아주 넓고 출구가 가늘다. 오른쪽(Trade show)은 입구가 좁지만 출구가 굵다. 각 출구 아래에 "$2,000", "$1,500", "$1,333" 라벨.

cards.title: The cheapest channel runs out.
body: The trade show happens twice a year, with a fixed crowd. Paying for a bigger booth won't double the buyers.
Ads work differently. Spend more and more inquiries arrive, though each one usually gets pricier as you reach less interested people.
list: What does one paying customer cost here?
How many more customers can this channel deliver?
cards.callout: Fill the cheapest channel until it stops giving, then move to the next.

cards.title: Early channel numbers are rough.
body: Nine customers is a small number. One big order or one bad show can swing the result.
Customers also touch several channels. A buyer who saw your ad, then visited your booth, gets credited to only one of them.
And some channels pay off slowly. Show contacts may buy months later. Judge a channel over a full buying cycle, not a single month.

cards.title: Now it's software for dental clinics.
body: Your scheduling app costs clinics $100 a month. Each $5,000 spent brought:
Search ads: 250 free trials, 20 paying clinics, staying about 6 months. A dental association newsletter: 50 trials, 15 paying clinics, staying about 24 months. Where should next quarter's budget go?

options.text: Search ads. Five times the trials for the same money
options.feedback: Trials aren't customers. Search customers cost $250 and bring about $600; newsletter customers cost about $333 and bring about $2,400.

options.text: The newsletter, as far as its audience allows, while keeping search running
options.feedback: You put money where each customer returns the most, and keep a channel that can grow once the newsletter's readers are used up.

options.text: Split the budget evenly to stay safe
options.feedback: It avoids betting wrong, but leaves your best channel underfunded while it still has room to grow.

cards.title: Compare channels by the customers they win, not the attention they get.
body: Cost per customer, what that customer is worth, and how many more the channel can bring. Those three numbers turn a channel debate into arithmetic.
**Try it today:** take your two main channels. Divide last quarter's spend on each by the paying customers it brought.
